title: RumourEngine
tagline: Rumours that spread from person to person, through towns, and across holds.
description:
As part of a larger project I'm working on, I needed a decent simulation of rumours spreading around the province. Now that I've got that working to the point I'm happy with it, and I've seen several other mods which might want to integrate something like this, I'm releasing it for the public.

On its own, it will take significant memories from NPCs and public-facing quest completions, and use them to create rumours in the area where it happens.
Then, they'll spread from rumourmill to rumourmill, across Skyrim, becoming slightly different with each retelling.
Once this happens, you'll start hearing NPCs occasionally talking about the latest things they've heard.

Conceptually this is similar to the feature in NarrativeEngine, except instead of injecting hundreds of memories which the embedding model may or may not bring up, it keeps its own list of rumours -- one copy per rumourmill -- and inserts them into SkyrimNet prompts.
It will also sometimes prompt "gossip" NPCs to talk about it when they're nearby, and no other conversations are happening, so you'll get a bit of flavour in the background, hopefully without it getting annoying; though if it does, there's a lot of settings in SkyrimNet's Plugin Settings you can use to customize it.

It's also a resource for other modders. It works out-of-the-box with mods which insert memories (like SeverActions off-screen events), but there's also an API other mods can use to create their own rumours about their world events. In the other project I've been working on, this has been incredibly immersive.

Feature list:
- Mills: NPCs are grouped into the circles that talk to each other daily. A town's commons, court, garrison and underworld each form one, and so do guilds and factions (the Legion, Stormcloaks, Thalmor, Companions, Dark Brotherhood, Volkihar, and more). The mills are built from your load order at every game start, so mod-added NPCs fit in on their own.
- Rumours from real events: every couple of game hours, recent SkyrimNet memories are screened by the decision model. It asks whether this person would pass it on, and how much of it they'd tell. What passes becomes a rumour, and the teller remembers spreading it, so you can catch the gossip.
- The player's deeds are fair game: whatever you get up to in front of people can come back to you, garbled, several towns later.
- Overhearing: anyone nearby when a rumour is told can carry it home.
- Quest endings become news: when one of your quests ends, its journal is read to judge whether word would get out, and how far. Dawnstar freed of its nightmares is talk in the Pale, and the Emperor's assassination is news everywhere. Thieves Guild business stays in the guild. quests.ini can set any quest to always or never.
- Spread over the map: rumours travel along roads, carriage routes, ships, shared members and informants, and the more notable ones travel faster. Small talk stays local, and big news crosses Skyrim.
- Retold at every stop: each mill's version is retold from the one it heard, by a cheap model, and only when someone there first needs it. Names blur, numbers grow, and each group adds its own slant.
- Who has heard it: not everyone in a mill knows everything. Gossips hear first, and trivia never reaches the tight-lipped. How much of a gossip someone is comes from their job and a reading of their SkyrimNet bio.
- Told as talk, not fact: rumours go into NPCs' bios as hearsay. Gossips raise them with each other, and with you and your followers in taverns by default; a setting changes where.
- Respects scenes: nobody gossips in the middle of an OStim or SexLab scene.
- Old news becomes history: when the biggest news has run its course, such as a war declared or a Jarl murdered, it becomes SkyrimNet world knowledge. Only the NPCs it actually reached get it.
- Followers bring stories home: a dismissed follower joins the mills of wherever they settle, and tells their tales of the road there. NPCs that other mods move to a new home are noticed the same way.
- Follows your setting: SkyrimNet's setting text goes into every rumour prompt, so what counts as scandal fits your Skyrim.
- Save-safe: there's no ESP and nothing is stored in saves. Each playthrough has its own database, and loading an earlier save takes back what happened after it. It can be added or removed at any time.
- Configurable: settings are on SkyrimNet's dashboard. mills.ini, gossips.ini and quests.ini can be patched by other mods with *_mills.ini-style files.
- API for mod authors: a stable v1 API in C++, Papyrus and ModEvents. Mods can add, update and retire rumours, give per-hold versions, set secrecy, delays and witnesses, issue proclamations, and ask what an NPC has heard.
- Cheap to run: retells and tellings use small, cheap models, and the README lists the models we've tried for each job.
author: maeyanie
changelog:
-"Quiet room" cooldown before gossip starts increased from 20s to 30s, and added a 60s cooldown after the player speaks.
-Tuned prompt to make people less likely to suddenly feel the urge to gossip mid-conversation.
-Encouraged people to talk about rumours where they were there as if they were there.
-Better support for Sofia and other difficult followers, plus an .ini to add more. If you encounter any, please let me know. Of all the ones I checked, only Sofia was broken.
